checks.name: the two runs are comparable (real, complete, dev, same model/settings/inputs/alerts/graph/policy/baseline; memory off + agent_v1 vs memory on + agent_v2_memory; clean isolation check; frozen log unchanged)
the comparison is of exactly these two runs
the comparison was not made with --allow-partial
the comparison schema is the expected one
the comparison covers every alert of both runs
the memory store loads, matches its manifest and passes the train-only checks
the memory store on disk is the one the memory-on run used (manifest hash)
the memory store was built from the current train.parquet (hash)
the memory-on run recorded a clean train/dev isolation check (0 overlapping flows)
the memory is seeded from the train split only (manifest says so)
the risk policy in the runs is the policy file now
the prompts in the runs are the registered prompts
agent_v1 is still the Week 3 locked prompt
the graph version in the runs is the code's graph version
every file locked by Week 3 is unchanged (42 files)
the Week 3 verification still passes (90 checks)
the migrations are numbered without gaps and checksummed (4)
the frozen unlock variable is not set
both runs recorded an unchanged frozen access log and unchanged Week 1 files
the frozen access log has no line added since the runs ended (line count equals the one the runs recorded)
no credential-like text in any locked artifact
the full-suite log exists
the full suite passed with no failures
the suite ran at least the Week 3 suite plus the Week 4 tests (>= 1097)
the log names every Week 4 test module (run it with -v)

actions.approval_note: Every proposed action starts as 'pending'. Approving or rejecting is a human decision made through the approval API; these runs contain none, so no approval rate exists and none is invented. Nothing is ever executed.

all_attacks_failures_wrong.population: all true attacks (no-verdict attacks count as wrong; lower bound)

coverage.population: true attacks with a valid verdict

attack_type.definition: Exact match of the predicted attack_type with the true class. A benign verdict on an attack counts as wrong.

on_attacks_flagged_malicious.population: true attacks the baseline called malicious

on_attacks_with_valid_verdict.population: true attacks with a valid verdict

benign_alerts_given_NONE.population: true benign alerts with a valid verdict (reported apart from MITRE accuracy)

coverage.population: true attacks with a valid verdict

mitre.definition: A predicted technique is correct if it is one of the accepted ids for the true class in the answer key (exact id match, no parent/child inference). Only true attacks are scored. A benign verdict gives technique NONE, which is never accepted for an attack, so it counts as wrong.

primary_on_attacks_with_valid_verdict.population: true attacks with a valid verdict (strict: the single primary id)

first_try_malformed.population: alerts that received at least one reply

recovered_by_retry.population: alerts whose first reply was malformed

retry_needed.population: alerts that received at least one reply

auto_closed_that_were_benign.population: auto-closed alerts (undefined when nothing was auto-closed)

routing.definition: Decisions of the risk policy recorded in each run, applied identically to both arms. 'no_routing' = the graph or policy produced no decision for the alert (never counted as closed).

true_attacks_auto_closed.population: true attacks (a closed attack is a missed attack)

true_benign_in_review_queue.population: true benign alerts (analyst workload that was not needed)

failures_escalated.definition: All alerts. An alert with no verdict stays escalated (counted as predicted malicious), as an analyst queue would treat an untriaged alert.

failures_wrong.definition: All alerts. An alert with no verdict is always counted wrong: an attack becomes a miss, a benign alert becomes a false positive. Worst case.

valid_only.definition: Only alerts that received a valid verdict. Alerts with no verdict are left out of the denominator.
